source.title: KAKURENBO: Adaptively Hiding Samples in Deep Neural Network Training
source.authors: Truong Thao Nguyen; Balazs Gerofi; E. J. Martinez-Noriega; François Trahay; Mohamed Wahib

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no apparent truncation or corruption.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports test accuracy after adaptive sample hiding and compares data-selection methods, but it does not test the listed claims about memorizing random labels, width, architecture, optimizer, dropout, sharpness measures, or removing memorized examples. Its batch-size experiment does not compare small- and large-batch generalization gaps under the conditions in V5.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test accuracy and training time for sample-hiding methods, but does not report training error or a training-to-test gap. It does not test the listed claim versions. Its batch-size results are included as related findings under fits_no_version, not as evidence for V5.
record.test_reason: Table 11 tests V5: ResNet-50(A) is trained for 100 epochs while global batch size increases from 1024 to 8192. Held-out accuracy is sufficient for V5; training error or a training-to-test gap is not required. The baseline uses learning-rate scaling and warmup and maintains accuracy, whereas KAKURENBO accuracy declines with larger batches.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the authors' conclusion: adaptive sample hiding reduces training time on large datasets while largely preserving prediction accuracy. This is conditional on the recipe and hiding fraction; it is not a demonstrated statistical equivalence across all settings.
record.recipe_differences: The study adaptively hides low-loss, confidently predicted samples, adjusts learning rate and hiding fraction, and measures test accuracy and training time; it does not use the original claim's interventions or measures.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports that accuracy changes with the maximum hiding fraction, prediction-confidence threshold, component combination, and batch size.

fits_no_version.finding: Adaptive low-loss sample hiding can preserve held-out accuracy while reducing training time; accuracy deteriorates with excessive hiding.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The accuracy and efficiency of adaptive sample hiding depend on dataset size, hiding fraction, and compensating training adjustments.

fits_no_version.finding: Removing the highest-loss 2% of DeepCAM samples increases KAKURENBO testing accuracy from 77.16 to 77.37 in Appendix D.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Excluding persistently high-loss samples can improve DeepCAM accuracy in the tested training recipe.

record.problems: Many reported results are single runs; the authors state resource limits prevented repeated runs for each data point. Uncertainty estimates are reported for only selected repeated-run results. Most reported metrics are test accuracy and training time, not the training-to-test gap relevant to the claim.
record.rows_left_out: No additional reported outcomes directly test the listed claim versions. Other method comparisons and training-time results were omitted because they do not report the training-to-test gap or another measure named by a version.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Width sweeps beyond the width required to interpolate.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and the contribution of local connectivity.
Controlled optimizer comparisons and tuning-dependent generalization.
Batches below 1024, language models, longer-training remedies, and an ablation isolating learning-rate scaling or warmup.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its correlation with generalization gaps, and comparisons with other measures.
Removal selected by label-memorization influence and comparison with equal-sized random removal. Low-loss hiding and highest-loss removal do not measure that selection criterion.

missing.what: Add explicit full-data baseline batch-size comparisons: accuracy 73.68, 73.98, 73.59 and 73.81 at batches 1024, 2048, 4096 and 8192. These are currently embedded only as baselines for method comparisons. Record the fixed 100 epochs, linear learning-rate scaling and five-epoch warmup.
missing.locator: Table 11; Appendix B.3, ResNet-50(A) recipe; Appendix C.3

record.verdict_notes: The record incorrectly treats a training-to-test gap as necessary for V5. Table 11 directly measures its named held-out outcome under a fixed epoch budget. The baseline's stable accuracy and KAKURENBO's declining accuracy require separate condition-specific verdicts. None of the other listed versions is tested.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Test error as network width increases beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected network generalization.
The study varies batch size while testing its sample-hiding method, but does not measure the training-to-test gap or compare large and small batches under the version's fixed-epoch conditions.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the generalization gap.

The study hides low-loss, confidently predicted samples; it does not select examples by how much their inclusion raises correct prediction or compare their removal against removing the same number of random examples as V8 specifies.

relationships.condition: ResNet-50(A), ImageNet-1K, KAKURENBO with maximum hiding fraction 0.4, 100 epochs, global batches 1024–8192.
relationships.reason: R8–R11 show accuracy declining from 73.60 to 73.21, 73.03 and 72.84 as batch size increases; repeated-run uncertainty is not reported for this sweep.
relationships.display_finding: The study reports progressively lower accuracy with larger batches, but these comparisons remain unverified and repeated-run uncertainty was unreported.

relationships.condition: ResNet-50(A), ImageNet-1K, full-data baseline, 100 epochs, learning-rate scaling and five-epoch warmup.
relationships.reason: Table 11's baseline sweep stays near 73.6–74.0 accuracy across batches 1024–8192, consistent with V5's adapted-recipe qualification; this verdict uses the text because R8–R11 store these results only as method-comparison baselines.
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy reportedly stayed near 73.6–74.0 across the batch sweep with learning-rate scaling and warmup, but these comparisons remain unverified.
